# storage-core: ArrayStorage contract, StridedBuf, Plain/Scalar/Any/View, Array read paths

Generated at commit bb1ee2c. Line numbers refer to that commit.

## Purpose

`ArrayStorage` (jix/src/storage/core_trait.rs:56) is the single trait every backend and lazy op
implements: `shape()`, `dtype()`, `read_data(index, ctx, out)` (pull / push) plus the hidden
`read_as_elementwise_pipeline`, `spec`, `info`, `as_compact`, `element_type_change`. `StridedBuf`
(buf.rs:44) is the byte buffer + per-dim `usize` byte strides that `read_data` returns and accepts.
Leaf backends here: `Plain` (plain.rs:64, zero-copy view of caller memory), `Scalar`
(scalar.rs:37, one value broadcast everywhere), `ArrayStorageAny` (any.rs:21, `Arc<dyn>`),
`View`/`Box`/`Rc`/`Arc`/`&dyn` forwarders (mod.rs:107-246). `Array<S>` (array.rs:173) adds the
front-end: `to_ndarray*`, `to_ndarray_slice`, `to_ndarray_buf` (+ request-splitting slow path),
`compact*` / `compact_fn*` and `compact_into_builder` (shared with `write_to*` in archive/array.rs:426).

## Contracts

Provided by this subsystem / required of every `read_data` impl (core_trait.rs:71-107):
- `index.len() == shape().len()`, each `start <= end <= shape[d]`, empty ranges allowed. Every
  impl must validate this itself (`check_get_range`, error.rs:212): `read_data` is a SAFE pub trait
  method, callable by users with arbitrary input. Plain (plain.rs:454), Scalar (scalar.rs:103) and
  Compact (compact.rs:278) do; the private `FnStorage` (array.rs:427) does not (only reachable
  through `compact_fn_with`, which passes valid chunk ranges).
- Every impl must call `check_out_buf` (buf.rs:282): it checks ONLY `out.strides().len() == ndim`
  and `out.is_writable()`. It does NOT check that `out`'s byte slice covers the region at its
  strides, nor that the strides do not alias. Nothing else does either (see Suspicions).
- Pull (`out=None`): return any buffer valid for the request shape at the returned strides: a
  read-only borrowed `Slice` of the storage's memory (Plain plain.rs:474, Scalar scalar.rs:112 with
  ALL-zero strides), or a writable pooled buffer (`materialize_out_buf`, buf.rs:309-317,
  laid out in `spec.read_layout_order()`). Pull bytes for the region must be initialized.
- Push (`out=Some(dst)`): write EVERY element of the region (including struct padding bytes) at
  dst's own strides starting at dst's byte 0, write NOTHING outside the region (dst's slice may be
  longer - test scalar.rs:217), return a view of dst (`view_mut`, buf.rs:272). Relied on for
  soundness by `to_ndarray_sub`'s `assume_init` (array.rs:800), by `compact_into_builder_dyn`,
  which hands `read_data` an uninitialized chunk buffer and then compresses all of it
  (array.rs:1366-1377), and by `read_data_and_map_strides`, which discards the inner return value
  in push mode and returns `out.view_mut()` (buf.rs:356-360).
- `read_as_elementwise_pipeline` default (core_trait.rs:123-135): `check_dtype` then pull read,
  wrapped by `unsafe OperandTyped::new_input` (contract elementwise_pipeline.rs:806-813: bytes are
  valid `T` values for the region). Scalar overrides it with a `Constant` node (scalar.rs:137-173).
- `shape()`/`dtype()`/`spec()` must be stable: `ArrayStorageAny` caches them at construction
  (any.rs:105-112) and `IntoType` asserts `inner.dtype() == ET::DTYPE` with `assert_unchecked_eq`
  (into_type.rs:88) after checking it once in `IntoType::new` (into_type.rs:59-61).
- `Array::dtype()` (array.rs:559-563) returns `S::ElementType::DTYPE` when static, else
  `storage.dtype()`; `to_ndarray_slice`/`to_ndarray_sub` size buffers with it while storages use
  their own `dtype()`. `ElementType` (element_type.rs:16) is a safe, unsealed pub trait.
- Spec invariants consumed here (block_shape > 0, `read_layout_order` and `read_shape_scale_order`
  are permutations of 0..ndim, read_size.min > 0, shape product fits u64) are only
  `debug_assert`ed in `Array::from_storage` (array.rs:1602-1631); `into_spec` hard-asserts a subset
  (params.rs:478-486); zero itemsize is rejected by `tune` (params.rs:307).

`unsafe fn` preconditions:
- `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts` / `from_raw_parts_mut` (pub, buf.rs:64, 84): `data` valid for
  `strided_span_bytes(shape, strides, itemsize)` bytes for `'a`; `_mut` also: strides do not alias.
  Caller = user / jix-py. The span helper zips shape with strides (util/mod.rs:109-118), so a
  length mismatch silently shortens the span; `stride * (len-1)` is unchecked.
- `from_slice` / `from_slice_mut` / `from_pool` / `with_strides` (buf.rs:102, 118, 131, 208):
  every access implied by strides AND the read shape it will be used with stays inside the slice;
  `_mut`/pool/with_strides: no aliasing strides. Callers: this subsystem + ops (they build sub-views
  of their own buffers). NOTE `with_strides` is used in pull mode by Broadcast (broadcast.rs:151)
  and keeps a writable PoolBuf writable while adding 0 strides.
- `copy_from` (buf.rs:221): both regions in bounds, src/dst non-overlapping (they become
  `PtrNoalias`/`PtrMutNoalias`; `NdCopier::copy` does no bounds checks, nd_copy.rs:47-53).
- `with_offset` (buf.rs:248): result valid for same shape/strides; `Slice`/`SliceMut` variants
  slice-index (panic if n > len), the `PoolBuf` variant defers the check to `data()`.
- `read_data_and_map_strides` (buf.rs:336): the stride-mapping closures produce valid strides for
  the inner region (push) / output region (pull). Callers: permute_dims.rs:127,
  insert_dim.rs:177, remove_dim.rs:162.
- `Plain::new` (plain.rs:116) / `Array::plain_ndarray_ptr` (plain.rs:422) /
  `Array::compact_nd_ptr` (array.rs:304): pointer non-dangling for the Plain's lifetime, every
  element of `0..shape[d]` at `strides` readable and a valid `dtype` value. Strides are unsigned
  byte strides; alignment is NOT required.
- `OwnedBlockTableBuilder::into_table` (block.rs:280, called array.rs:1213): no written contract;
  implicitly every block 0..nblocks was written and decoder dtype matches `ET`.

## Unsafe inventory

- core_trait.rs:134 `OperandTyped::new_input` - dtype equality checked at :132; validity of bytes
  is the read_data pull contract (non-local).
- buf.rs:71, 91 `slice::from_raw_parts(_mut)` with computed span - caller contract (user).
- buf.rs:102-136, 208-259 constructors/relabels - callers; no runtime check at all.
- buf.rs:229-239 `NdCopier::copy` - in-bounds and non-overlap rely on callers (Plain push
  plain.rs:476, Scalar push scalar.rs:128, Broadcast push); dst bound is the user `out` (NOT
  established, see Suspicions).
- buf.rs:316 `from_pool` - pool buffer >= product*itemsize bytes (buf_pool.rs:40-51); product is
  an unchecked `usize` multiply (buf.rs:312).
- buf.rs:351, 364 `from_slice_mut` + lifetime `transmute` - justified locally (out is None in
  the pull branch so the inner can only borrow self/context, both `'a`). Non-local: push branch
  assumes the inner wrote through `inner_out`.
- any.rs:64 `assert_unchecked(len <= NDIM_MAX)` - established by `DimDyn::from_slice` ->
  `assert_dim` at construction (any.rs:108 -> dimension.rs:165-166 -> error.rs:133-151).
- scalar.rs:111, 125 `cast_slice::<T,u8>` of `self.data` - exposes T's padding bytes (uninit for
  padded `#[repr(C)]` structs) as `&[u8]`; scalar.rs:120 `cast_slice_mut::<u8,T>` - alignment
  asserted (util/mod.rs:211, panic not UB), length bounded by the `[..region_len]` slice.
- scalar.rs:148 `transmute_copy::<T,T2>` - `check_dtype` at :145 plus the `unsafe trait Dtyped`
  layout promise (dtype.rs:1147-1155).
- plain.rs:187 `SendSyncPtr::new` - makes Plain Send+Sync whenever `A` is (util/mod.rs:529-531).
- plain.rs:254 `ptr.add(offset)` from ndarray - established by ndarray.
- plain.rs:469-471 `ptr.add(in_offset)` + `from_raw_parts(src_ptr, src_span)` - relies on
  Plain::new contract + `check_get_range` + strides being the true non-negative byte strides
  (NOT established for negative ndarray strides, see Suspicions); empty region uses base ptr.
- plain.rs:289 / 294 `plain_ndarray_ref_impl` / `plain_ndarray_ptr` - lifetime tied to `&'a`
  ArrayBase (sound for data lifetime), strides computed with `as usize` (see Suspicions).
- array.rs:459 / 464 FnStorage typed `write` / `write_unaligned` - aligned path guarded by
  dtype.alignment() check of base and strides (446-448); dtype.alignment() >= align_of::<T>()
  holds for built-in scalars on every target (dtype.rs:969-982 hard-codes 8 for 64-bit types even
  on i686) and for derived structs; offset in-bounds is the push contract.
- array.rs:791-800 `from_raw_parts_mut` over the uninit ndarray, `from_slice_mut`, `assume_init`
  - relies on every element being written (non-local: every storage's push path).
- array.rs:851 `from_slice_mut` - buf length checked exactly by `check_get_buffer_size`
  (error.rs:241-247; 32-bit hole, see Suspicions).
- array.rs:1061-1062 `from_slice_mut(&mut out_buf[out_offset..])` - slicing is bounds-checked
  at the start only; writes rely on `out` covering the whole request.
- array.rs:1213 `into_table` - see above.
- array.rs:1369, 1405, 1433-1435 `AlignedBytes::set_len` without init - chunk relies on push
  filling every byte; block relies on `fill(0)` for partial blocks and a full copy otherwise;
  compressed buffer relies on `encode` returning a length <= bound.
- array.rs:1374-1376 `from_slice_mut` over chunk_buf with packed chunk strides - local.
- array.rs:1418-1427 `get_unchecked(src_byte_offset..)` + `copier.copy` - local arithmetic:
  `block_in_chunk_idx*block_shape < chunk_size` per dim.

## Edge-case surface

- Empty ranges / zero-length dims: `NdCopier::copy` returns early (nd_copy.rs:64); Plain uses the
  base pointer with span 0 (plain.rs:463-465, test plain.rs:530); Scalar contiguous path has
  region_len 0; slow path returns before the heuristic (array.rs:1030-1032); `to_ndarray_sub` gets
  ALL-zero strides from ndarray when any extent is 0 (test array.rs:2328); compaction of an empty
  array iterates no chunks and builds nblocks=0.
- 0-d (shape []): `product()` = 1 so `nitems` = 1 (small read); slow path dispatch Dim<0>
  (array.rs:994); compaction dispatch falls to DimDyn (array.rs:1269, test compact_fn_0d);
  `strided_span_bytes([])` = itemsize; Scalar fast path fills 1 element.
- Length-1 dims: Plain::new treats len<=1 as "don't care" in layout order (plain.rs:150, 171);
  `is_contiguous` demands exact default strides, so a len-1 dim with another stride is reported
  non-contiguous (conservative).
- Broadcast 0-stride: Scalar pull = all-zero strides; Plain accepts 0 strides (ndarray broadcast
  views) and orders them outermost (plain.rs:151-168); out buffers may not have 0 strides on
  len>1 dims (doc only, never checked); pull results of Broadcast stay writable with 0 strides.
- Permuted / padded / offset `out`: honored everywhere via `out_strides`; `to_ndarray_sub`
  allocates in `read_layout_order` (array.rs:767-787) so results can be F-order.
- NDIM_MAX: `dim_arr` asserts <= 8 (dimension.rs:526) - panics, never UB; ndarray inputs with
  ndim > 8 get TooManyDimensions (plain.rs:515).
- Unaligned: never required. Only FnStorage and Scalar take aligned paths and both check.
- Struct dtypes / inner shape: copies are by (itemsize, alignment) class (nd_copy.rs:31-39):
  (8,4) as `[u32;2]`, (16,8) as `[u64;2]`, others bytewise; padding bytes are copied as data.
- bool: `to_ndarray_sub::<bool>` `assume_init`s whatever bytes the storage produced; a TypeDyn
  archive re-tagged with `into_typed::<bool>()` is never validated for 0/1 in this subsystem.
- f16 / complex: no special handling here beyond the copy class (f16 (2,2), c32 (8,4), c64 (16,8)).
- 32-bit targets: unchecked u64->usize at array.rs:436, 764, 960, 1022, 1058, 1366; plain.rs:458,
  467; scalar.rs:115; error.rs:246-247; `Idx::from_u64` is a plain `as` (util/mod.rs:86-88) so
  `default_strides` in `to_ndarray_slice` (array.rs:850) truncates too; buf.rs:312 product*itemsize.
  Lazy views (broadcast, scalar, compact_fn) make huge regions cheap to request.
- Integer edges: index math is u64 and bounded by validated ranges; `nitems` u64 product can only
  overflow for shapes that skipped `check_shape_overflow` (Scalar::new, compact_fn shapes - tune
  does not check, params.rs:299-330); then debug panics in `from_storage`, release wraps.
- Aliasing out vs input: only reachable through the unsafe constructors (Plain over memory that a
  user `out` also covers); the jix-py `out=` boundary is the py concept unit's job.

## Intentional behaviors

- `to_ndarray`/`to_ndarray_sub` may return non-C-contiguous ndarrays in the storage's hinted
  layout (docs array.rs:585-589, 642-645; tests array.rs:2355, 2385).
- No alignment is required of `out` or promised for returned buffers (core_trait.rs:97-101,
  buf.rs:20-22, plain.rs:97-100; tests plain.rs:740, array.rs:2299).
- Pull may return a read-only view of the storage's memory or a buffer with broadcast 0 strides
  (core_trait.rs:78-80); a read-only `out` and a wrong stride count are rejected with
  InvalidArgument (buf.rs:282-297, test array.rs:2473).
- Push writes only the region; bytes after it in a larger slice stay untouched (test scalar.rs:217).
- `to_ndarray_slice` requires the EXACT byte length (doc array.rs:807-809, error.rs:250).
- Invalid index is reported before an ndim mismatch in `to_ndarray_sub` (test array.rs:2528).
- Zero-sized dtypes are rejected (params.rs:307, test params.rs:1853).
- `compact_fn` visits elements in arbitrary order (array.rs:324-326); compaction zero-pads
  boundary blocks (array.rs:1232-1233, 1406-1408).
- `ArrayParams` never change how a Plain buffer is stored (plain.rs:90-95); `maybe_compact_with`
  ignores params when already compact (array.rs:1577-1580).
- `to_ndarray` builds and drops its own ReadContext (array.rs:579-583), so Warn-mode arithmetic
  warnings (overflow/underflow by default, codec/mod.rs:418-421) are not observable through it.
- `from_storage` validates the spec only under `debug_assertions` (array.rs:1602-1631).
- Python rejects negative strides explicitly (jix-py/src/ops/common/operand.rs:177); the
  `StridedBuf`/`Plain` model has no negative strides by design (buf.rs:47).

### Changed in c009869 (#87) - supersedes conflicting statements above (line numbers above refer to bb1ee2c)
- `check_out_buf(out, shape, index, itemsize)` now also checks index ndim, the 32-bit region size
  (`check_region_size`: prod(index) * itemsize <= isize::MAX on 32-bit), and that out's slice covers
  the furthest byte the region touches (non-empty regions). K14 / K16 are fixed.
- `check_shape_overflow` also caps every dim at i64::MAX.
- The assert_unchecked in IntoType and Op2::shape were removed. The pipeline uses fewer lanes when
  the itemsize exceeds the SIMD width.
- Python numpy(out=...) documents that out must not overlap any numpy array in the lazy chain.

### Changed in 4d11918 (#90) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- `ArrayStorage` is sealed: every impl needs an `ArrayStorageImpl` marker, so user code cannot
  implement it and the unsafe code may trust read_data's buffers (K50 fixed).
- `check_out_buf` calls `check_get_range` before anything else (K61). Pull buffers whose strides
  alias (0-stride broadcast) are returned read-only (K58). Plain constructors return an error for
  negative strides (K45). `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts(_mut)` documents its full safety contract.

## Hot spots

- Push-mode buffer size: is there ANY path from safe code that makes a push write past `out`'s
  slice? `check_out_buf` has no size check, `StridedBuf` carries no shape, `NdCopier` has no
  bounds checks, and pull results (`from_pool`, writable) can be fed back as `out`.
- `to_ndarray_buf_slow_dyn` (array.rs:1010-1066): are the pieces disjoint and covering for an
  unaligned start, a read_shape that `scale_read_shape` snapped to `array_shape`
  (util/mod.rs:521-525), and partial last pieces? `read_shape >= 1` comes from the clamp at
  util/mod.rs:488; piece bounds from `NdIterExtBlockOffsetSize::new` (iter/block.rs:46-80) with
  `calc_block_end` (util/mod.rs:609-617). Does `out_offset` (1057-1059) match the piece start for
  permuted out strides?
- `small_read` (array.rs:964): `plain_read` storages (Plain, Scalar, and InsertDim/RemoveDim/IntoType
  /View/Any which keep the flag, insert_dim.rs:211, remove_dim.rs:196) are never split. Slice's
  pull fast path (slice.rs:145-159) assumes a plain_read pull view is valid for its bounding box.
- `compact_into_builder_dyn` (array.rs:1274-1442): block_index (1378-1398) vs grid order; chunk
  boundary blocks; `full_block` skip of zero-fill relies on the copy covering the whole block;
  uninit chunk_buf + push contract; dispatch for ndim 5..8 and 0 via DimDyn.
- `to_ndarray_sub` (array.rs:743-801): `inv_order` construction (779-785) is right only if
  `read_layout_order` is a permutation (debug-only check); `assume_init` needs full coverage.
- `read_data_and_map_strides` (buf.rs:336-368): lifetime transmute and the push-mode assumption
  that the inner storage wrote into `inner_out` rather than returning another buffer.
- Plain construction from ndarray (plain.rs:243-262, 284-294): negative strides, `into_raw_vec_and_offset`.
- Two paths that must agree: Scalar `read_data` vs `Constant` pipeline; Scalar contiguous vs
  strided push; Plain pull view vs push copy; small_read vs slow path (same bytes, different
  layout); `to_ndarray_slice` vs `to_ndarray_buf` vs `to_ndarray_sub`.
- Recent churn: #75 (75fd25b) removed the `D: Dimension` generic and rewrote ~400 lines of
  array.rs (slow path and compaction now dispatch on runtime ndim); #72 (763a701) moved the index
  check out of `to_ndarray_buf_checked` into its three callers (debug_assert left at array.rs:958)
  and bounded Scalar's fill to `region_len`; #70 (623bcd6) added Box/Rc/Arc forwarders.

### Suspicions (unverified)

- buf.rs:282-297 / array.rs:938-946 - `out` span never checked against the request: in safe code,
  `let mut b = a.view().neg().to_ndarray_buf(&[0..1, 0..1], &ctx, None)?;` (writable PoolBuf,
  elementwise_pipeline.rs:879) then `big.to_ndarray_buf(&[0..100, 0..100], &ctx, Some(&mut b))`
  should make NdCopier/Compact write far past the 4-byte pool allocation (heap overflow, no unsafe).
- error.rs:246-247 (via array.rs:848) - on 32-bit `product as usize` and `nitems * itemsize` wrap,
  so `to_ndarray_slice` on a cheap lazy array with >= 4 GiB region accepts a tiny `buf` and the
  read writes past it; same family: array.rs:764 (per-dim truncation sizes the ndarray smaller
  than the region read) and buf.rs:312 (pull allocation size wraps).
- plain.rs:289 - `s as usize * size_of::<T>()` on a negative ndarray stride (`a.slice(s![..;-1])`,
  `invert_axis`): debug overflow panic, release wraps to a huge stride and plain.rs:461-471
  builds a bogus `from_raw_parts` length / `ptr.add` offset (UB) from safe `plain_ndarray_ref`,
  `plain_ndarray_view` and `compact_ndarray` (array.rs:274); plain.rs:248 panics for owned arrays.
- element_type.rs:16 + array.rs:559-563 - a user `ElementType` impl whose `DTYPE` and `dtype()`
  disagree makes `to_ndarray_slice` size-check with one itemsize while Plain writes with the other
  (safe trait relied on by unsafe code; contrived, low).
- scalar.rs:111 / plain.rs:476 / array.rs:1366-1435 - `#[derive(Dtyped)]` structs with padding:
  padding bytes are uninit, yet they are viewed as `&[u8]`, copied as integers by NdCopier's
  `[u32;2]`/`u64` classes and fed to the encoder (Miri-level uninit reads; low).

## Review units

Paths below are under jix/src unless they start with jix-py/.

- storage-core-buf-contract: core_trait.rs:1-173, buf.rs:1-368, mod.rs:1-298, any.rs:1-113,
  info.rs:1-74 (~1030 lines). Consult util/nd_copy.rs, util/buf_pool.rs, util/mod.rs,
  ops/shape_ops/{permute_dims,insert_dim,remove_dim,broadcast,slice}.rs, ops/into_type.rs,
  storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs. Focus:
  - Can safe code make a push read write outside `out`'s slice (check_out_buf has no size check;
    pull PoolBufs are writable and can be passed back as `out`)?
  - Is the transmute in `read_data_and_map_strides` sound for every caller, and does the push
    branch hold if the inner returns a buffer other than `inner_out`?
  - Which callers of `with_strides`/`from_pool`/`with_offset` can create writable aliasing (0)
    strides or an offset beyond the slice?
  - `materialize_out_buf`: usize product overflow (32-bit), non-permutation layout orders.
  - `is_contiguous(_aligned)` exactness for len-0/len-1 dims and itemsize % alignment != 0.
  - Forwarders (View/Box/Rc/Arc/&dyn/Any): any method left at its default that changes behavior
    (the `&dyn` impl uses the default `read_as_elementwise_pipeline`); Any's cached metadata.
  - Is the documented contract of `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts(_mut)` sufficient?
- storage-core-leaf-backends: plain.rs:1-518, scalar.rs:1-194, array.rs:177-509 (~1045 lines).
  Consult storage/buf.rs, util/mod.rs, util/nd_copy.rs, storage/params.rs, element_type.rs,
  dtype.rs, util/iter/strides.rs. Focus:
  - Negative / odd ndarray strides into plain_ndarray(_ref/_view) and compact_ndarray.
  - Plain::read_data span/offset math for empty ranges, end-of-dim starts, len-1 and 0-stride dims.
  - Scalar push fast vs strided path, and `read_data` vs the `Constant` pipeline (bool, structs).
  - FnStorage: missing index validation, aligned-write decision, NdIter offsets relative to start.
  - Padding bytes of derived struct dtypes through Scalar/Plain/NdCopier.
  - Plain's derived `read_layout_order` is always a permutation.
  - Unsafe constructor contracts: null ptr for empty shapes, Send/Sync via SendSyncPtr.
- storage-core-array-read-paths: array.rs:511-1716 (~1205 lines). Consult storage/buf.rs,
  storage/params.rs, util/mod.rs, util/iter/{block,strides}.rs, error.rs, storage/block.rs,
  storage/compact.rs:268-330, archive/array.rs:388-430, archive/block.rs. Focus:
  - Slow-path pieces: disjoint, covering, correctly offset into permuted/padded `out`.
  - `to_ndarray_sub`: layout permutation, strides, and what could leave `assume_init` holes.
  - 32-bit truncation in `to_ndarray_slice` size check and `to_ndarray_sub` shapes.
  - Compaction: block_index mapping, padding, uninit chunk buffer, `get_unchecked` bound, 0-d.
  - `small_read` bypass for plain_read storages; error paths with partially written state.
  - What `into_table` assumes and whether `compact_into_builder` guarantees it.
